text: Dian Cécht was the master of leechcraft for the Tuatha DÉ Danann. He knew the site of a spring called the Well of Slaine. That spring healed every wound except beheading. Healing gods were common among the Celts. Dian Cécht was an Irish form of the healing water gods. Roman legions used the name Apollo for those gods through the interpretatio romana. Dian Cécht failed to heal Nuada after a battle. The fight against the FOMORIANS took place on the plain of MAG TUIRED. An enemy cut off Nuada's arm completely. A severed limb lay beyond Dian Cécht's skill. A blemished king could not reign. Nuada yielded the throne of TARA to Bres mac Elatha. Bres was half-Fomorian and evil. The Tuatha DÉ Danann asked Dian Cécht to try again. Dian Cécht built a full arm of silver for Nuada. Nuada became known as Nuada of the Silver Arm. That still was not enough. Dian Cécht's son MIACH healed Nuada fully. Miach made skin grow over the silver. Dian Cécht killed Miach in fury. AIRMID tended Miach's grave. Hundreds of herbs grew there, one for each part of the body. As Airmid sorted them, Dian Cécht destroyed her work. That act removed the secrets of healing from the land. Dian Cécht became MAC CÉCHT. He married the land goddess FÓDLA.
objective: Dian Cécht was the healer god of the Tuatha DÉ Danann. He knew the healing spring Well of Slaine.
key_results: The Well of Slaine healed every wound except beheading.
After Nuada lost his arm, Dian Cécht built a silver replacement but could not save the throne.
Dian Cécht's son MIACH healed Nuada completely before Dian Cécht killed him.
Dian Cécht destroyed his daughter AIRMID's work and hid the secrets of healing.
evidence: Monaghan, The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
